This improves some recent results. † † footnotetext: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 30D45, 30D30, 30D20, 30D35. † † footnotetext: Key words and phrases: Value distribution theory, Meromorphic functions, Differential monomials, Differential polynomial 1.

arxiv-2109-02753.title: End-to-end Neural Information Status Classification
arxiv-2109-02753.creator: Yufang Hou
arxiv-2109-02753.description: Abstract Most previous studies on information status (IS) classification and bridging anaphora recognition assume that the gold mention or syntactic tree information is given Hou et al. 2013a ; Hou 2016 ; Rösiger et al. 2018 ; Hou 2020b ; Yu and Poesio 2020 . In this paper, we propose an end-to-end neural approach for information status classification.

arxiv-2206-02285.title: Story Beyond the Eye: Glyph Positions Break PDF Text Redaction
arxiv-2206-02285.creator: Maxwell Bland, Anushya Iyer, Kirill Levchenko
arxiv-2206-02285.description: Abstract . In this work we find that many current redactions of PDF text are insecure due to non-redacted character positioning information. In particular, subpixel-sized horizontal shifts in redacted and non-redacted characters can be recovered and used to effectively deredact first and last names.

arxiv-2307-05150.title: A Modal Logic for Explaining some Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2307-05150.creator: Pierre Nunn and Francois Schwarzentruber
arxiv-2307-05150.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a modal logic in which counting modalities appear in linear inequalities. We show that each formula can be transformed into an equivalent graph neural network (GNN). We also show that each GNN can be transformed into a formula. We show that the satisfiability problem is decidable.

arxiv-2401-14702.title: FairSample: Training Fair and Accurate Graph Convolutional Neural Networks Efficiently
arxiv-2401-14702.creator: Zicun Cong, Baoxu Shi, Shan Li, Jaewon Yang, Qi He, Jian Pei
arxiv-2401-14702.description: Abstract Fairness in Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs) becomes a more and more important concern as GCNs are adopted in many crucial applications. Societal biases against sensitive groups may exist in many real world graphs. GCNs trained on those graphs may be vulnerable to being affected by such biases.

arxiv-2410-02516.title: Learning Emergence of Interaction Patterns across Independent RL Agents in Multi-Agent Environments
arxiv-2410-02516.creator: Vasanth Reddy Baddam, Suat Gumussoy, Almuatazbellah Boker, Hoda Eldardiry
arxiv-2410-02516.description: Abstract . Many real-world problems, such as controlling swarms of drones and urban traffic, naturally lend themselves to modeling as multi-agent reinforcement learning (RL) problems. However, existing multi-agent RL methods often suffer from scalability challenges, primarily due to the introduction of communication among agents.

arxiv-2410-24178.title: AR-Pro: Counterfactual Explanations for Anomaly Repair with Formal Properties
arxiv-2410-24178.creator: Xiayan Ji *, Anton Xue *, Eric Wong, Oleg Sokolsky, Insup Lee
arxiv-2410-24178.description: Abstract Anomaly detection is widely used for identifying critical errors and suspicious behaviors, but current methods lack interpretability. We leverage common properties of existing methods and recent advances in generative models to introduce counterfactual explanations for anomaly detection. Given an input, we generate its counterfactual as a diffusion-based repair that shows what a non-anomalous version should have looked like .

arxiv-2502-11985.title: Variational Quantum Algorithms for Many-Body Systems
arxiv-2502-11985.creator: Mirko Consiglio
arxiv-2502-11985.description: Abstract \Acp VQA incorporate hybrid quantum–classical computation aimed at harnessing the power of NISQ ( NISQ ) computers to solve challenging computational problems. In this thesis, three main VQA are presented, each tackling a different facet of many-body physics. The first is the VQE ( VQE ), which is designed to determine the ground-state of the extended Fermi-Hubbard model.

arxiv-2511-07061.title: Do LLMs Feel? Teaching Emotion Recognition with Prompts, Retrieval, and Curriculum Learning
arxiv-2511-07061.creator: Xinran Li, Yu Liu, Jiaqi Qiao, Xiujuan Xu
arxiv-2511-07061.description: Abstract Emotion Recognition in Conversation (ERC) is a crucial task for understanding human emotions and enabling natural human-computer interaction. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown great potential in this field, their ability to capture the intrinsic connections between explicit and implicit emotions remains limited.

arxiv-2512-10596.title: Beyond Pixels: A Training-Free, Text-to-Text Framework for Remote Sensing Image Retrieval
arxiv-2512-10596.creator: Jinghao Xiao, Yiheng Guo, Xing Zi, Karthick Thiyagarajan, Catarina Moreira, Mukesh Prasad
arxiv-2512-10596.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jinghao Xiao, Yiheng Guo, Xing Zi, Karthick Thiyagarajan, Catarina Moreira, Mukesh Prasad. Semantic retrieval of remote sensing (RS) images is a critical task fundamentally challenged by the “semantic gap” , the discrepancy between a model’s low-level visual features and high-level human concepts. While large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) offer a promising path to bridge this gap, existing methods often rely on costly, domain-specific training, and there is a lack of benchmarks to evaluate the practical utility of VLM-generated text in a zero-shot retrieval context.

pmc-11497523.creator: Wensheng Zhang, Kun Zhang
pmc-11497523.description: Objectives:For prostate cancer (PCa), hundreds of risk variants have been identified. pmc-13203742.title: A Low-Parameter Adaptive Framework Based on Gaussian Mixture Modeling for Detecting Weak Astrocytic Calcium Signals in Two-Photon Imaging
pmc-13203742.creator: Jiameng Xu, Huiquan Wang, Shaofan Yang, Xiang Liao, Kuan Zhang, Guang Zhang
pmc-13203742.description: Two-photon microscopy enables in vivo imaging of astrocytic Ca2+ activity, yet detecting weak, transient, and background-coupled signals remains challenging due to low signal-to-noise ratios and heterogeneous noise. uslaw-usc-t42-s1395b.title: 42 U.S.C. § 1395b — Option to individuals to obtain other health insurance protection
uslaw-usc-t42-s1395b.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s1395b.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 7 (Social Security); Subchapter XVIII (Health Insurance For Aged And Disabled). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Nothing contained in this subchapter shall be construed to preclude any State from providing, or any individual from purchasing or otherwise securing, protection against the cost of any health services.
